CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Tyler is a 56-year-old male presenting with difficulty swallowing that began 4-5 weeks ago. He reports a sensation of something being stuck in his throat, which is occasionally painful. The difficulty is primarily with solid foods such as sandwiches and steak, requiring him to wash them down at times. He reports no difficulty with liquids and denies any temperature-related changes with hot or cold liquids. He has not fully choked but is concerned about potential choking. He denies hemoptysis, hematochezia, vomiting, weight loss, chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing with swallowing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or other side effects from metformin. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Norvasc (amlodipine)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neck: No swelling, thyroid normal, no masses, no lymphadenopathy. Throat: No masses, swelling, or redness visualized. Carotid: No bruits. Lungs: Clear to auscultation. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Abdomen: Epigastric tenderness noted, no masses or significant swelling. Back: Normal. Extremities: Normal. Neurological: Normal.

RESULTS
Blood pressure: 120/50 mmHg. Last hemoglobin A1c: 7.4. Morning blood sugar readings reported within target range approximately 80% of the time. Home blood pressure readings reported on range or close to target.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Difficulty swallowing, suspected esophageal stricture or narrowing. Referral to gastroenterology for esophagoscopy and evaluation. Start Prilosec 20 mg once daily. Advised to chew food thoroughly, especially solids. Instructed to proceed to emergency department if food becomes completely impacted. Patient to call office if symptoms worsen. Diabetes mellitus: Repeat hemoglobin A1c ordered. Chemistry panel ordered including kidney function. Referral to ophthalmology for diabetic retinopathy screening. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily. Follow-up visit in one month to review laboratory results and adjust medications if needed. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled. Continue Norvasc. Refill sent to pharmacy. Patient instructed to call with any concerns.
